title: Center for Functional Nanomaterials
content:
The Center for Functional Nanomaterials (CFN) is a US Department of Energy Office of Science user facility at Brookhaven National Laboratory in Upton, New York, providing universities and industry access to state-of-the-art nanoscience instrumentation with staff scientist support. Capabilities include a Materials Synthesis and Characterization Facility (solution-phase, CVD, PVD and ALD synthesis), five transmission electron microscopes, proximal probes for in situ surface studies, a class 100/1000 cleanroom nanofabrication facility, and theory and computation resources, in close synergy with the NSLS-II synchrotron on the same campus.

For aerogel and nanostructured materials developers, the CFN offers advanced synthesis and nanoscale characterization via peer-reviewed proposals or proprietary cost-recovery projects.
